title: One Ångström Inside the Cellular Telephone Switchboard — Martin Rodbell's 1971 Contaminated ATP Bottle, Alfred Gilman's S49 cyc- Gs Purification, Cholera Arg201 & Pertussis Cys351 Locks & the 35% GPCR Pharmacopoeia (PDB 1TND, 1GP2, 3SN6, 1AZS)

teenKit.tldr: Over a third of all modern medicines target the exact same molecular bottleneck in your cells called GPCRs, a discovery sparked by a contaminated lab bottle in 1971.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It explains why completely different conditions like asthma, heart arrhythmias, and obesity can be treated by drugs plugging into the same microscopic switchboard.
keyTakeaways: About 35% of all FDA and EU approved drugs operate through just 134 specific G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs).
Martin Rodbell discovered the GTP switch mechanism in 1971 by realizing that dirty, contaminated horse-muscle ATP was actually making cell experiments work.
Bacterial infections like cholera and pertussis hijack these exact same cellular switches by locking them in an "on" or "off" state.

vocab.meaning: A massive family of protein sensors embedded in cell membranes that act like a universal remote control to pass outside chemical signals into the cell.
A cellular energy molecule that acts like a microscopic battery pack to flip molecular switches on and off.
A famous lab-grown mutant cell line missing a key relay piece, which scientists used like a blank canvas to isolate and purify the missing protein.
A high-tech imaging method that shoots X-rays at crystallized proteins to map their atomic 3D structures down to an Ångström.

quiz.question: What percentage of modern FDA and EU approved drugs operate through GPCRs according to the 2018 Sriram and Insel study?
quiz.explanation: The study revealed that roughly 700 drugs—about 35% of all approved medicines—target just 134 specific GPCRs.

quiz.question: How did Martin Rodbell figure out that GTP was the hidden trigger for cell signaling in 1971?
options: By analyzing a lucky chemical impurity in dirty horse-muscle ATP
By designing a mutant cell line from scratch
By accident while boiling water in a beaker
quiz.explanation: Rodbell realized that a trace contamination in unpurified horse-muscle ATP was the actual active ingredient driving the cell's response.

quiz.question: What do cholera and pertussis toxins actually do inside the human body?
options: They chemically lock GPCR switches in permanent 'on' or 'off' positions
They drain all the water out of the cell
quiz.explanation: Cholera and pertussis hijack the system by chemically modifying specific amino acids (like Arg201 and Cys351) to freeze the G-protein switches.
